--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.is_planar()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Check if the graph is planar. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.is_planar()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Check if the graph is planar. title: >- [Graph.is_planar()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Check if the graph is planar. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if the graph is planar. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L25453-L25559){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.is_planar() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Is planar](../assets/graphs/is-planar.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: the complete graph on four nodes drawn with D inside triangle A B C, so no edges cross and is_planar() returns True. Right: the complete bipartite graph K3,3, nodes A, B, C each joined to D, E, F, drawn with a single crossing, marked in the accent color. Its 9 edges are within the 3n - 6 bound of 12, but no drawing avoids every crossing, so is_planar() returns False." width="100%"} A graph is planar if it can be drawn in the plane without any two edges crossing. This is an exact test: it runs the left-right planarity test (Brandes' formulation of de Fraysseix and Rosenstiehl's criterion) in linear time, like NetworkX's `is_planar()`. Edge direction, self-loops and parallel edges make no difference to planarity, so they are ignored. Use `check_planarity()` to get a crossing-free arrangement of the edges around each node when the graph is planar, or the Kuratowski subgraph that rules it out when it is not, and `layout_planar()` to draw a planar graph without crossings. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph is planar, `False` otherwise. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~check_planarity`) : The test with its certificate: an embedding or a Kuratowski subgraph. [](`~layout_planar`) : Positions that draw a planar graph without edge crossings. ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Euler's formula $n - e + f = 2$ for a connected planar drawing, together with every face of a simple planar graph being bounded by at least three edges, gives the edge bound $e \le 3n - 6$ for $n \ge 3$. A graph above the bound is rejected at once; otherwise a depth-first search orients the edges and the test checks whether its back edges can be split into a left and a right side without conflicts. By Kuratowski's theorem a graph is planar exactly when it contains no subdivision of $K_5$ or $K_{3,3}$, so graphs that pass the edge bound can still be non-planar: $K_{3,3}$ has 9 edges against a bound of 12, and the Petersen graph 15 against 24. ## Examples {.doc-examples} `K_4` is planar: draw one node inside the triangle of the other three. `K_5` is not; its 10 edges are already more than `3 * 5 - 6 = 9`. `K_{3,3}` is not planar either, although it is well inside the edge bound: ::: {#4219114e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec ( ec.Graph().add_full_graph(n=4).is_planar(), ec.Graph().add_full_graph(n=5).is_planar(), ec.Graph().add_complete_bipartite_graph(3, 3).is_planar(), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, False, False) ``` ::: ::: ### A floor plan The rooms of a two-story office, joined where a door leads from one to the other, can be drawn as they're laid out in the building, with no two doors crossing: ::: {#b5a21e3c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} offices = ec.offices() offices.is_planar() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Drawn at the rooms' positions on the plan, the second floor above the first: ::: {#12abde29 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} offices.plot( layout="pos", color_by="kind", label_by="label", width=700, height=520 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### The smallest non-planar graphs `K_5` and `K_{3,3}` are the two smallest graphs that aren't planar, and every non-planar graph contains a copy of one of them, with its edges perhaps stretched into paths. `K_5` is on the left and `K_{3,3}` on the right. However their nodes are placed, the drawing has at least one crossing: ::: {#fd8c3ede .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} k5 = ec.Graph().add_full_graph(n=5) k33 = ec.Graph().add_complete_bipartite_graph(3, 3) k33.layout_bipartite(nodes=[1, 2, 3]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` Number of nodes : 6 Number of edges : 9 Directed : False Density : 0.60 Average degree (min, max) : 3.00 (3, 3) Connected : True Number of connected components : 1 Tree : False Bipartite : True Computations: - layout_bipartite(nodes=[1, 2, 3]) -> attr: 'pos' (6 of 6 nodes) ``` ::: ::: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#95225a89 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} k5.plot(layout="circular", width=320, height=320, legend=False) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {#5ae82578 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} k33.plot(layout="pos", width=320, height=320, legend=False) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: They're only just non-planar: deleting any one edge makes either planar: ::: {#07ee5abd .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} k5.delete_edge(1, 2) k33.delete_edge(1, 4) k5.is_planar(), k33.is_planar() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ``` (True, True) ``` ::: :::
